title: Leaky Database Transactions (Infrastructure Pollution)
pattern: Core business or domain logic classes directly initiate, commit, or rollback database transactions, coupling transaction boundaries to database connections.
why_bad: It tightly couples the business rules to specific database persistence technologies and infrastructure. If you migrate from a SQL database to a microservice API or NoSQL store, the domain logic cannot be reused.
detection: Methods in core domain services importing, referencing, or calling database-specific transaction primitives (like SQL transaction queries).
counterexample: Pure infrastructure implementation layers (like repositories or database adapters) where managing transactions is their explicit responsibility.
fix: Manage transaction boundaries at the application service or middleware layer, keeping the core domain logic entirely database-agnostic.
source: Vaughn Vernon, *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* (2013), Chapter 4 ("Architecture" / Transaction bounds).
